name: Client Intake and Triage
title: Client Intake and Triage
answer: Client intake and triage in legal operations covers the first contact a prospective client has with a firm or legal department, through conflict checks, matter classification, urgency scoring, eligibility screening, and routing to the right practice group or fee earner. It also includes capturing contact details, consent, and the facts of the matter in a structured way, then deciding whether the matter is accepted, declined, or referred. In an AI context, the scope extends to automated questionnaires, document upload, identity verification, and the use of language models to summarize or categorize incoming requests. The boundary is the point where a human lawyer must make a professional judgment about acceptance, conflict, or legal advice.

sections.heading: Scope

sections.body: The infrastructure for AI-assisted intake typically runs on a practice management system or client relationship management platform, a secure client portal, and a document management system. It may include identity verification services, e-signature tools, and cloud APIs that connect forms to conflict databases and matter management. Language models and classification services can sit behind the portal, often through a vendor or a private cloud instance, with data stored in a structured intake record. Security controls include encryption, access roles, audit logs, and data residency settings, because intake data often contains personal and privileged information.
sections.heading: What it runs on

sections.body: The work is done by combining rules, forms, and machine learning. A prospective client fills in a guided questionnaire, uploads documents, and the system extracts names, dates, parties, and subject matter. A classifier or language model then scores the matter for urgency, practice area, and potential conflict, and routes it to a queue for a human reviewer. Staff and lawyers review the output, correct errors, and record the decision, so the model supports rather than replaces professional judgment. Over time, the intake team may tune thresholds and prompts using historical outcomes, but the final acceptance decision remains with a qualified person.
sections.heading: How the work is done

sections.body: Rights and risk and provenance in intake and triage center on confidentiality, privilege, conflict of interest, bias, and data protection. The system must show where data came from, who touched it, and which model version produced a summary or score, so an audit trail exists for later disputes. Vendor contracts, consent notices, and retention schedules matter because intake data can include sensitive personal information and privileged communications. The site tracks 219 compliance and regulation pages and 6948 state AI bills, which reflects how many different rules can apply to automated intake across jurisdictions. Bias testing and human review are common controls, because a triage model that systematically deprioritizes certain matters or clients can create legal and reputational exposure.
sections.heading: Rights, risk and provenance

sections.body: The direction of travel is toward more integrated, agentic intake that can verify identity, check conflicts, draft an engagement letter, and open a matter with less manual handoff. Firms are likely to see deeper links between intake, court deadline calculators, and knowledge management, with models that explain their routing decisions. Regulation and case law will continue to shape what can be automated, and the site's tracking of 148 active AI lawsuits, 92 of them intellectual property, and 29 AI case law precedents suggests that disputes over data and model use will inform intake design. The likely steady state is a hybrid process, with automation handling volume and structure while lawyers retain control over acceptance, advice, and client communication.
